Remember that boiling a nitrile with aqueous NaOH gives a sodium carboxylate, so intermediate Q must be propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$.
To swap $\text{Cl}$ for $\text{CN}$ by nucleophilic substitution, you need a good source of $\text{CN}^-$ ions in a solvent that favours substitution over hydrolysis.
walkthrough:
**Compare start and finish to spot chain lengthening**

Great detective work starts with counting carbons. Chloroethane is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ (2 carbons) and sodium propanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$ (3 carbons).

So the first step must add one carbon atom:

**Work backwards from Q to identify it**

We are told Q is hydrolysed with boiling aqueous NaOH to give the carboxylate salt. That is the classic nitrile hydrolysis.

$$\text{R-CN} + \text{NaOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{R-COO}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{NH}_3$$
So for $\text{R} = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2$, Q must be propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$.

**Choose the reagent to make the nitrile**

To get $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$ from $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, we need nucleophilic substitution of $\text{Cl}$ by $\text{CN}^-$:

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{Cl}^-$$
We need ionic cyanide, $\text{KCN}$, dissolved in ethanol. Ethanol favours substitution and avoids the aqueous hydrolysis to an alcohol.

options.A: Concentrated ammonia gives nucleophilic substitution to an amine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (ethylamine). This does not add a carbon and cannot be hydrolysed to propanoate.
options.B: Dilute sulfuric acid would hydrolyse a haloalkane to an alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. This keeps 2 carbons and gives no nitrogen to later form the carboxylate.
options.C: Hydrogen cyanide in water is a weak acid and a poor source of $\text{CN}^-$ for substitution of a chloroalkane. HCN is used for addition to carbonyls, not for this substitution, and water would favour formation of ethanol instead.
options.D: Potassium cyanide provides $\text{CN}^-$ for nucleophilic substitution to form propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$. Using ethanol (not water) prevents hydrolysis to the alcohol and ensures the nitrile forms, which then hydrolyses to sodium propanoate.
